approaches.name: integrated national digital health information and surveillance systems
approaches.description: The project deploys interoperable health information, surveillance, laboratory, emergency and telemedicine systems to track patients and threats nationwide. Practices: Integrated One Health digital surveillance system for human and animal health; Nationwide electronic medical records for continuous patient monitoring; Telemedicine and tele-appointment systems for underserved areas; Integrated pre-hospital and hospital coordination system with bed management; Integrated early warning system consolidating health, animal and environmental data; Laboratory Information Management System for test result tracking and sharing; AI pattern-recognition diagnostics and point-of-care testing in labs; National PHC management information system deployment; Multi-level PHC indicator dashboard from health information system; Mobile and telemedicine services for primary care CSBs; Integrated health MIS with data-protection-by-design; CSB connectivity for DMI and EVAX vaccine tracing; National health identifier for interoperable health MIS; Integrated DMI, e-pharmacy and cold-chain systems at CSB; Computer-aided dispatch with priority algorithms and real-time GIS; Automated ambulance fleet management system; Emergency department triage information system; Bed management information system for patient transfers; Geo-mapping analysis of climate-vulnerable health access disparities; Early warning systems for emerging infectious diseases; National information system for medical equipment lifecycle management; bed management system in hospitals; PHC information systems deployed in CSBs; laboratory information system scaled to regional hospitals and CSBs; national disease surveillance and response management system; GIS geomapping of emergency service 30-minute coverage; unique ID system connecting CSB patient records; national integrated surveillance system capturing all cases; PHC information systems (DMI, Evax, ePharmacie, HRH) in health centers; hospital bed management system across 33 hospitals; climate-sensitive disease early warning system linked to shock alerts; geomapping methodology for climate-vulnerable PHC access planning; digitized medical records and EVAX immunization system at PHC; CHVA-data-driven pre-hospitalization and SMUR coverage design; Digitized bed management system for specialized care.

evidence.text: Component 1 focuses on strengthening health system resilience to protect citizens' health through the implementation of an integrated One Health surveillance system for both human and animal health.

extra_evidence.text: This digital approach enables better monitoring and response to health threats, directly supporting the PNS goal of citizen protection.

Within this component, digital health serves as a key enabler: telemedicine development facilitating specialized care access in underserved areas; nationwide electronic medical records implementation for continuous patient monitoring; generalized tele-appointment systems across health establishments; and digitalization of frontline structures including electronic medical records for chronic disease management and vaccination tracking.
Component 3 reinforces emergency and hospital services by implementing a coordination system for pre-hospital and hospital services that integrates bed management.

This technological enhancement reduces waiting times and optimizes patient care, aligning with the recommendation of PNS to provide the public sector with necessary resources to effectively fulfill its missions and strengthen care availability.

Specifically, this subcomponent will support the following activities. • Development of an Integrated EWS: This system will consolidate data from multiple sectors, including health, animal and environmental monitoring, into a single platform for comprehensive analysis and response coordination.
The subcomponent will incorporate climate and meteorological indicators into the EWS and surveillance systems, where feasible, to better detect and respond to climate-related health risks.

This will involve activities such as strengthening early warning and surveillance systems (EWS), improving data sharing and information exchange, and fostering capacity building across relevant sectors.

Key activities under this subcomponent will include: • Laboratory Equipment and Infrastructure Upgrades: This will include the provision of state-of-the-art laboratory equipment and the modernization of up to 14 laboratory facilities to improve testing capabilities, including the procurement of diagnostic tools, equipment for microbiology, biochemistry, and hematology, as well as carrying out minor works to support advanced diagnostic functions. • Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS): the LIMS will be strengthened to improve data management and reporting, and enable the efficient tracking, storing, and sharing of laboratory test results, improving data accessibility and quality assurance.

This includes incorporating emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, for pattern recognition in diagnostics, point-of-care testing, and rapid diagnostic tools for infectious diseases.
The subcomponent will adopt an innovative approach, ensuring that laboratories have access to diagnostics and testing technologies.

It will do so through three subcomponents: i) strengthening the organizational structure and governance of PHC and strengthening human resources for health at the PHC level through reorganization plans at each of the circonscriptions; ii) upgrading the capacity of CSBs based on the PHC service reorganization plans at each of the circonscriptions; and iii) supporting the deployment of a comprehensive national PHC information system.

Reorganization plans will determine priority quality indicators to be captured, and the information system that will be deployed under sub-component 2.3 will implement a dashboard at the central, regional, local, and facility level to these track indicators.
The activities will include the acquisition and installation of medical equipment to improve essential services as well as the implementation of mobile and telemedicine services.

This subcomponent will help deploy a unified/integrated Management Information System (MIS), to improve the collection, use, and processing of health data; it will be implemented taking a data protection-by-design and -by-default approach, as defined in the Project Operations Manual (POM).
Sub-component 2.3 will support the deployment of a comprehensive and integrated health information system (US$23 million).

This sub-component will also improve the internet connectivity of up all CSBs to deploy the front-line DMI and the national vaccine portal (EVAX) to trace vaccination to protect against climate-sensitive diseases, in particular against influenza or tuberculosis.

The Project will support the deployment of the national health identifier that will ensure the interoperability of the health MIS with other sectors and while ensuring the protection and privacy of personal data as well as strengthening cyber security measures.
This includes the deployment of DMI at the CSB level, appointment scheduling systems, implementation of a referral and counter-referral system, and telemedicine services.

Information systems for managing the cold chain, medication management (e-pharmacy), equipment management, human resources will also be integrated, which will improve monitoring and evaluation and decision-making.
This includes procuring fully equipped ambulances and implementing a Computer Aided Dispatch system with priority dispatch algorithms and real-time GIS.
An automated fleet management system will ensure optimal maintenance of the ambulance fleet through scheduled preventive maintenance and reports on overall fleet condition.
This subcomponent will optimize reception and triage in emergency departments through a dedicated information system to guarantee efficient care and reduce overcrowding in hospitals.
A new bed management information system will be put in place to ensure a smooth and efficient transfer of patients from emergency departments to other services.

An ongoing Geo-mapping analysis and an assessment of the vulnerability of the health sector to climate will identify women and girls’ disparities in access, who live in hard-to- reach areas, locations prone to flooding and extreme heat making it difficult to access health services.

The reorganization plans will be designed to address these challenges and improve equitable access to health services; the plans will also prioritize women’s burden of disease such as women that have high risk pregnancies, NCDs, medical complications, among others.

It will address emerging infectious diseases, improve laboratory capacity and develop robust early warning systems, and enhance emergency services to effectively respond to medical emergencies arising from extreme weather events.

The Project will build upon key deliverables from the COVID-19 Response Project (P173945), including the national information management system for medical equipment, which will facilitate the monitoring of procurement, delivery, and maintenance of medical devices.
